topic: Ottoman land army size (modern historians' range - low end synthesis)

note: Stated as the low end of a 'more realistic' 60,000-80,000 modern range, contrasted explicitly with the Sphrantzes figure.

topic: Ottoman land army size (modern historians' range - high end synthesis)
attributed_to: World History Encyclopedia summarizing modern historians
note: High end of the same 60,000-80,000 modern range.

topic: Ottoman land army size (infobox figure, same article as CL04)
note: Infobox figure conflicts with the body text of the same article (see CL04).
Popular narrative history; composition given as about 70,000 regulars plus 20,000 irregulars (90,000 total), a figure between the World History Encyclopedia range and the EBSCO figures.

topic: Ottoman land army size (Ottoman archival data, unverified attribution)
attributed_to: Saint Andrew Greek Orthodox Church blog, attributing to unspecified 'recent studies and Ottoman archival data'
note: Cited only to show the range is echoed outside academic publishing; the specific archival attribution could not be verified in this project.

attributed_to: George Sphrantzes (4,773 Greeks + about 200 foreigners, as translated on De Re Militari)
note: This is the De Re Militari translation's wording. A different wording of the same tradition (4,983 Greeks + just under 2,000 foreigners) circulates in later and secondary retellings; see CL09. Sphrantzes says the emperor asked him to keep the true number secret.

topic: Byzantine/allied defenders (variant wording of the Sphrantzes tradition)
attributed_to: Popular retellings (e.g. a devotional blog quoting 'the Chronicle') citing 4,983 Greeks and just under 2,000 foreigners
tier: Tier 3 (secondary paraphrase; also associated with the later Pseudo-Sphrantzes / Chronicon Maius tradition, which BMCR (S42) identifies as a 16th-century text once misattributed to Sphrantzes)
note: Kept separate from CL08 because the underlying figures differ (4,983 vs 4,773 Greeks; ~2,000 vs ~200 foreigners) and because of the Pseudo-Sphrantzes attribution risk documented in S42.
Rounds the Sphrantzes-tradition figure down as an upper bound ('fewer than').
Body text gives about 7,000; see CL12 for the same page's conflicting infobox figure.

topic: Byzantine/allied defenders (infobox figure, same article as CL11)

Stated as the combined length of the city's walls that the defenders could not adequately cover; presented as a round figure, not a survey measurement.
5.7 km figure for the main Theodosian triple-wall line specifically (narrower scope than CL13's full-circuit figure).

topic: Theodosian land-wall length (broader scope, includes Blachernae extension)
note: Likely includes the northern single-wall Blachernae extension in addition to the main triple line, which would explain the gap with CL14.
Matches CL14's 5.7 km figure via an independent popular source, offering weak corroboration.

topic: Ottoman ships transferred overland into the Golden Horn

tier: Tier 1/3 (corroborated across a scholarly reference and a popular synthesis)
note: The two sources independently converge on approximately 70 ships, which raises confidence in this specific figure relative to the Sphrantzes total fleet figure (CL18).

topic: Ottoman total fleet size (sea side, contemporary chronicle figure)

Most reportedly belonging to Italian colonists of the city rather than to Byzantine forces proper.

attributed_to: Multiple sources converge on 6 April to 29 May 1453 inclusive
note: Most common figure when counting from the conventional 6 April opening-bombardment date to the 29 May fall.
Longer count likely reflects a different start date (e.g. the 2 April arrival of the main army, per C12) rather than a factual disagreement about when the city fell.

attributed_to: World History Encyclopedia gives 500 kg; TheCollector gives 550 kg
note: Close but not identical figures; kept as a range rather than resolved to one number.
